errorCodes.meaning: The caller does not hold the community-administrator capability. Linked accounts are not namespace-scoped — a member's account is linked once, community-wide, and used wherever their rights reach — so holding git.ns.admin on a namespace does not entitle a caller to this list.

AccountRow.description: One member's account on one forge, as linked through git-ns/account/link.

account.description: The linked account. `id` is authoritative; `login` is as the forge last reported it — display only.

linkedAt.description: When the VTC recorded the link. Absent for a link recorded before this member was tracked.

member.description: The member the account is linked to.

memberCurrent.description: Whether `member` is still a current member. One whose access lapsed keeps the link — nobody else may link the account — but it projects no forge role, and a forge role it holds cannot be adopted as a right.

AccountRow.title: AccountRow

Did.description: A bare DID in the W3C DID Core syntax (§3.1): `did:`, a method name of lowercase letters and digits, `:`, and a method-specific id of colon-separated segments drawn from `A-Z a-z 0-9 . - _` and percent-encoded octets, the last segment non-empty. A DID URL is not a DID: no path, query or fragment (`/`, `?`, `#`), so a verification-method id such as `did:key:z6Mk…#z6Mk…` is refused. Compared by exact string equality — no case folding or percent-decoding. A consumer MUST still treat the value as data: the pattern keeps shell metacharacters, whitespace and quotes out of the wire form, but it does not make a DID safe to splice into a command or markup.
Did.title: Did

Ext.description: Vendor-namespaced extension object per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Each immediate key MUST be a reverse-DNS namespace; structure under each namespace is opaque to the framework.
Ext.title: Ext

ForgeAccount.description: A person's account on one forge. `id` is authoritative; `login` is for display only, because logins can be renamed and re-registered.

login.description: The account's current login, as the forge reported it when last seen. Display only.

ForgeAccount.title: ForgeAccount

ForgeHost.description: The lowercased DNS host of a forge: `github.com`, a GitHub Enterprise Server host, `codeberg.org`, or a self-hosted Forgejo instance such as `git.example.org`. No scheme, no port, no path. The host is a segment of every resource, so a right never crosses forges.
ForgeHost.title: ForgeHost

ForgeId.description: An identifier the forge itself assigns — a repository id, a user or organisation id — carried as a string so a forge whose ids are not numbers needs no new version. GitHub and Forgejo ids are decimal integers written as strings (`"812736451"`). Unlike a name, it survives renames and transfers, which is why rights and bindings are keyed by it.
ForgeId.title: ForgeId

Response.description: The matching links, ordered by member then forge.

accounts.description: Links matching `member` and `forge`, ordered by `member` then `account.forge`. At most one per member per forge.

nextCursor.description: Continuation token for the next page; pass it back as the request's `cursor`. Absent on the last page — never `null`.

schema.description: A community administrator lists every member's linked forge accounts, community-wide. The outer document members (id, type, issuer, recipient, issuedAt, expiresAt, proof) are owned by the framework — SPEC §6.3.

cursor.description: Opaque continuation token from a previous response's `nextCursor`. A consumer supplying a `cursor` MUST NOT also change `member` or `forge` from the request that produced it — start a fresh query instead.

forge.description: Only accounts linked on this forge. Absent: every forge.

limit.description: Maximum accounts to return in this page. A VTC clamps to 1..=500 (default 100).

member.description: Only this member's linked accounts. Absent: every member.

schema.title: Git Namespaces — List Linked Forge Accounts — payload
